items.abstract: This article examines how algorithmic management and neurotechnologies transform occupational risks and the employer’s duty of prevention. Drawing on a legal review of publications from 2015 to 2025 and a doctrinal, functional, and comparative analysis, it examines psychosocial, cognitive, discriminatory, and other risks associated with the processing of neural data. The study compares the safeguards established under European law, International Labour Organization standards, and the Peruvian legal framework governing occupational safety and health, data protection, and artificial intelligence. It identifies difficulties in assessing risks arising from opaque systems, supervising automated decision-making, and safeguarding workers’ right to defend themselves against disciplinary measures. The article proposes clarifying preventive obligations through the provision of clear and comprehensible information, meaningful human involvement in decisions producing significant effects, participatory risk assessments, and limits on the processing of mental data. In the Peruvian context, it distinguishes existing legal obligations from proposed regulatory measures.

items.title: Not All Fakes Are Equally Ugly: The Anti-AI Bias in Aesthetic Judgment and the Role of Affect, Self-Relevance, and Authenticity
items.abstract: Art is devalued once it is attributed to artificial intelligence (AI). Whether this anti-AI bias is a generic penalty for non-original works or specific to the absence of a human author is unknown, as is how long it lasts. In a preregistered study, 324 participants rated 48 genuine human paintings, each presented as an Original, a human Forgery or AI-Generated, on beauty, valence, meaningfulness and monetary worth, then judged how synthetic (AI vs. human) and authentic (copy vs. original) each was. Forgeries were rated below Originals on every dimension, and AI-Generated works about twice as low, the AI-specific penalty falling most heavily on meaningfulness. The labels did not alter gaze, and their effects did not depend on the emotional content or personal relevance of the artworks. Artworks labelled AI-Generated were judged more synthetic and, less clearly, Forgeries less original, and the more beautiful an artwork, the more likely it was judged human-made, even when unlabelled. About six weeks later (n = 220), after learning that all artworks were human originals, participants no longer rated previously AI-labelled works as less beautiful. They had forgotten the labels but remembered what they had believed, and reconstructed the labels from these beliefs and their initial appraisal. The bias tracked attitudes toward AI, not interoceptive sensibility or visual imagery. The anti-AI bias thus combines a generic non-originality penalty with a penalty specific to the missing human author: it acts at the moment of judgment, yet leaves beliefs that outlast the memory of the label.

items.title: Occupational stress and its association with burnout, turnover intention and patient- safety outcomes among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital, Sierra Leone: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Occupational stress affects not only healthcare-worker wellbeing but also organisational stability and patient safety. Evidence linking occupational stress to these downstream outcomes is scarce for Sierra Leone. This study examined the association between occupational stress and burnout, turnover intention, absenteeism and patient-safety outcomes among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 healthcare workers selected by stratified proportionate random sampling. Occupational stress was measured with the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) and treated as the exposure. Outcomes were burnout dimensions (emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation, reduced personal accomplishment), self-reported turnover intention, absenteeism exceeding three days per month, and patient-safety events (medication errors and near-miss incidents in the preceding three months). Associations were assessed using Pearson's chi-square tests in SPSS v26, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results Among workers with high occupational stress, emotional exhaustion was present in 61.2%, reduced personal accomplishment in 53.8% and depersonalisation in 44.7%. Turnover intention was substantially higher among highly stressed workers than among those with low or moderate stress (56.4% vs 22.1%; χ² = 38.4, df = 1, p < 0.001), as was absenteeism exceeding three days per month (38.2% vs 14.6%). Patient-safety outcomes were also elevated: 22.7% of highly stressed workers reported a medication error and 31.5% a near-miss incident in the preceding three months, compared with 8.9% and 12.3% respectively among less-stressed workers. Conclusions High occupational stress is strongly associated with burnout, intention to leave and patient-safety events among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital. Occupational stress is therefore both a workforce-wellbeing and a patient-safety concern, and institutional psychosocial support, retention strategies and safety-culture interventions are warranted. items.title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
items.abstract: Hallucination research in low-resource languages fragments easily: each newly named failure mode prompts its own dataset, spending scarce annotators on incomparable resources. We argue for consolidation and test it at community scale. Alikbachan is a Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark stratified along three crossed axes: a human-validated cultural-distance band, six task types, and a five-family, 32-mode hallucination taxonomy. It comprises a harvested 2,516-item test set (Phase 1) and a quota-constructed, gold-labeled 5,000-item set (Phase 2). The stratification is diagnostic. Four zero-shot LLM judges vary by over 30 macro-F1 points across strata, and the item-level predictions of 99 Phase-1 and 32 Phase-2 competition systems reproduce the profile: discourse-level omission defeats judges and most teams alike, whereas only a minority over-flag negative controls. The judges' verdict probabilities rank items well (ROC-AUC 0.74-0.95) but are overconfident (ECE 0.04-0.29). An open competition on Alikbachan drew 222 teams and 3,566 submissions, and a single-prompt 32B judge reaches the 57th percentile. Of the 25 teams in both phases, 24 regress on Phase 2 (mean $-17.6$ points) while every zero-shot judge improves, and Phase-1 rank barely predicts Phase-2 rank (Spearman $ρ=0.35$), so a Phase-1 leaderboard alone would have crowned a different winner.

items.title: OpenDesk AI: An Intelligent Desktop Assistant for Natural Language-Based File Search, System Monitoring, and Task Automation
items.abstract: Modern computer operating systems require users to navigate multiple menus, folders, and applications to complete everyday tasks. This process can be time-consuming and challenging, especially for users with limited technical knowledge. This research paper presents OpenDesk AI, an intelligent desktop assistant designed to simplify computer interactions using Natural Language Processing (NLP). The system allows users to perform tasks such as searching for files, monitoring CPU and memory usage, managing applications, and automating routine desktop activities through natural language commands. OpenDesk AI follows a local-first architecture, where user data and system operations are processed locally to improve privacy, security, and response speed. The proposed system uses intent recognition and entity extraction to understand user commands and execute the corresponding operations through operating system interfaces. It combines natural language understanding with system monitoring and task automation to provide a more accessible and efficient computing experience. The experimental results reported in this study show an intent classification accuracy of 94.6% and task execution time reductions ranging from 84% to 89.12% compared with traditional manual operations. These findings suggest that OpenDesk AI can improve user productivity, reduce repetitive manual work, and provide a practical approach to privacy-focused desktop automation. Keywords: Desktop Automation, Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Intent Recognition, Semantic File Search, System Monitoring, Local-First Architecture, Human-Computer Interaction.

items.title: Organic Framework Nanozymes for Smartphone-Assisted Sensing: Material Design, Catalytic Strategies, Signal Transduction, and Applications
items.abstract: Organic framework nanozymes, encompassing metal–organic, covalent–organic, and emerging hydrogen–bonded organic frameworks, are investigated as catalytic materials for portable sensing. Their tunable metal nodes, organic ligands, pore structures, defect sites, and supramolecular microenvironments enable the construction of peroxidase-, oxidase-, catalase-, hydrolase-, and laccase-mimetic activities. Meanwhile, smartphones can assist these systems by providing image acquisition, illumination, RGB/HSV color analysis, fluorescence recording, chemiluminescence capture, data processing and portable quantitative readout, allowing conventional laboratory assays to be transformed into on-site sensing platforms. This review summarizes recent progress from 2022 to 2026 in smartphone-assisted organic framework nanozyme sensing platforms, with emphasis on catalytic signal generation, framework design, smartphone-assisted image processing, and applications in biomedical analysis, food safety, and environmental monitoring. Furthermore, the review delves into the main challenges and future directions, including in-depth analysis of catalytic mechanisms, enhancement of selectivity, standardization of imaging techniques, signal modulation assisted by artificial intelligence, device integration, and performance validation in real samples. This review aims to provide practical guidance for the development of organic framework nanozyme sensing platforms that combine catalytic signal amplification, portability, and smartphone-assisted optical analysis, thereby promoting their application in real-time detection and on-site analysis.

items.title: PACMNET V4, N4, December 2026 Editorial
items.abstract: The Proceedings of the ACM on Networking (PACMNET) series showcases top-tier research in emerging computer networks and their applications. We welcome submissions introducing new technologies, innovative experiments, creative applications of networking technologies, and fresh insights gained through analysis. Supported by the ACM Special Interest Group on Communications and Computer Networks (SIGCOMM), the journal is backed by a distinguished Editorial Board composed of leading researchers in the field. This issue constitutes the fourth issue of the fourth volume of PACMNET and features articles submitted to the June 2026 deadline that were accepted. This issue marks the completion of PACMNET's fourth year and reflects the journal's steady growth and increasing maturity. Since its launch in 2023, the number of published research articles has grown from 24 in its first year to 32 in 2024, 50 in 2025, and 60 in 2026. A total of 172 submissions were received for this cycle and underwent a rigorous review process involving 95 Editors, coordinated by two Associate Editors. During the initial phase, each submission received a minimum of three reviews. Submissions that progressed to the second phase were evaluated through at least two additional reviews per article. Following a second round of reviews, the Editors convened online to determine which submissions should be accepted with minor revisions subject to shepherding, which should be invited for a one-shot major revision, and which should be rejected. At the conclusion of this process, 25 articles were accepted, with the authors asked to implement minor revisions under the guidance of a shepherd and included in this issue of PACMNET. The articles in this issue span programmable data planes, Internet infrastructure and transport protocols, and network measurement. Contributions on in-network intelligence include model reconfiguration, adaptive packet classification, and collective communication, alongside transport research on congestion control for distributed training, TCP pacing, and microburst elimination. Measurement studies cover DNS interception, NTP infrastructure, 5G handover inefficiencies, cellular interference, shared IP addresses, and P2P monitoring, while satellite networking contributions examine LEO routing and the suitability of Starlink for live video. Additional work addresses censorship evasion, DoS defense, eBPF diagnostics, BGP traffic engineering, and optical control planes. Collectively, these papers reflect the growing convergence of machine learning, systems design, and large-scale measurement in modern networking research. As usual, we would like to express our sincere gratitude to all those who contributed to this issue of PACMNET, especially the Authors for submitting their finest work and the Associate Editors for offering valuable feedback in their reviews and engaging in the discussions. Our thanks also go to the SIGCOMM Executive Committee Chair and the CoNEXT Steering Committee members for their continued support and guidance, providing essential suggestions and insights throughout the article selection process.

items.title: PAIR-MED: Policy-reward Alternation for Iterative Refinement in Multilingual Medical Reasoning
items.abstract: Large language models demonstrate strong medical question-answering capabilities, yet reasoning performance remains uneven across languages. Process reward models (PRMs) provide step-level feedback for improving reasoning, but a fixed PRM may become increasingly misaligned with the trajectory distribution of an evolving policy during reinforcement learning, thereby reducing the reliability of its supervision. We propose a policy--reward alternating training framework that jointly adapts a medical PRM and optimizes a multilingual reasoning policy. Following supervised initialization, the current policy generates multilingual trajectories to update the PRM, which then provides process-level rewards for the next policy update. Medical step supervision maintains the PRM's medical foundation, while process, outcome, and language-related rewards guide policy learning. We develop multilingual medical PRMs (PAIR-PRM) and reasoning models (PAIR-MED) at 8B and 9B scales across 12 languages. On the medical subsets of Global-MMLU and MMLU-ProX, our models improve average accuracy by 3.01--7.47% over their corresponding Qwen backbones. On CUREMED-BENCH, PAIR-MED-9B improves the joint language consistency and logical accuracy metric by 12.88% and 7.45% over baselines for in-domain and out-of-domain languages. Further analyses examine PRM adaptation, multilingual reasoning quality, and the contributions of individual training components.

items.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
items.abstract: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable. In particular, we show that given some dangerous program, no algorithm can predict whether an agent will run such a program that is semantically equivalent. In general, guardrails, blacklists, whitelists and certifications can only lead to imperfect safety solutions. Under finite constraints (bounded context, values and running time) safety is decidable but still intractable. Specifically, the problem is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even when the description of the agent is known. Finally, safety is not a compositional property, i.e., agents that can be proven safe on their own can still produce unsafe behavior when grouped together. We also discuss relaxed notions of safety that could be used in practice.

items.title: Perceived-Severity Hierarchy and Rating Disagreement in Korean Unethical Utterances: Harmfulness Judgments Are Not Reducible to Sentiment
items.abstract: Toxic language detection for large language model safety has largely been framed as binary classification, yet unethical expressions differ in severity across types and human judgments of severity are far from uniform. We analyze a large-scale Korean ethics-verification corpus with eight type labels (seven unethical types plus neutral) and the individual intensity votes (0–3) of five raters per sentence (363,154 sentences; 1,001,030 votes). First, the seven unethical types form a three-tier perceived-severity hierarchy—censure (1.42) < discrimination, hate, and abuse (1.53–1.59) < sexual, violence and crime incitement (1.74–1.75)—supported by post-hoc tests: all between-tier differences are significant with substantial effect sizes (Holm-corrected p < 0.05; |Cliff’s δ| = 0.14–0.45), while within-tier effects are negligible. Second, automatically estimated sentiment valence barely explains the hierarchy (Spearman ρ = −0.142; AUC = 0.621; replicated with a Korean-specific sentiment model and with preceding dialogue context included in the input); the two most severe types show the most neutral surface valence, so sentiment signals capture best precisely the least severe type. Third, inter-rater agreement is low (ordinal Krippendorff’s α = 0.373), yet the disagreement is not explained by the basic demographics the corpus records—rater gender and age (equivalence tests bound the pooled gender effect at |d|≤0.013 and the age correlation at |ρ|≤0.002; unrecorded rater characteristics remain untested)—and instead grows with item severity (sentence-level ρ = 0.248). Harmfulness judgment appears to be a dimension largely independent of sentiment, whose annotation may benefit from continuous scales, multi-rater averaging, and severity-proportional rating resources.

items.title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
items.abstract: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.

items.title: Physician AI disclosure, condition severity, and public trust in digital medicine
items.abstract: Public trust is central to the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital medicine, yet little is known about how patients respond to different forms of physician AI disclosure across clinical risk contexts. In a 5 × 2 factorial experiment in mainland China, 1574 adults were randomly assigned to physician profiles varying by AI use type and condition severity. Administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI across physician perception and care-seeking intention outcomes. High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that competence, trust, and empathy accounted for different disclosure-related response patterns. Main effects were directionally consistent in a supplementary offline community sample from Macao ( n = 128). These findings suggest that AI disclosure in digital medicine should distinguish administrative from clinical uses and be calibrated to clinical severity, while highlighting the need for preregistered replication using behavioral outcomes.

items.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
items.abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

items.title: PILAPS: A Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Pragmatic Inference across Phenomena and Settings
items.abstract: Recent work reports strong pragmatic performance by large language models (LLMs) in English, yet whether this performance generalises across languages and evaluation settings remains unclear. This question is increasingly important as LLMs are deployed across languages, cultures, and conversational contexts. In this paper, we first introduce PILAPS, a bilingual English/Mandarin Chinese benchmark covering eight pragmatic phenomena across purpose-written and dialogue-derived items, with both culturally adapted and independently sourced data. We then evaluate eight LLMs from four families across a range of model sizes and prompting strategies. Our results reveal substantial variation across models and pragmatic phenomena: open-source models continue to struggle particularly with humour, while cross-linguistic performance varies with model origin. Our error analysis shows that, compared with human participants, models are more prone to literal interpretations in conversational contexts. Theory-of-Mind prompting lowers the literal share of errors, whereas Chain-of-Thought prompting slightly raises it. Together, these findings demonstrate that strong pragmatic performance in one evaluation setting does not necessarily generalise across languages or conversational contexts.

items.title: PlanWise: An AI-Powered Personal and Collaborative Task Management System
items.abstract: Effective task and project management needs efficient task prioritization, scheduling, progress monitoring, and coordination among people, all things considered. Conventional task management systems mostly rest on manual planning and tracking, which can make it difficult for users to manage competing priorities and changing workloads. This paper introduces PlanWise, an AI-powered personal and collaborative task management system designed to support task organization, project coordination, and intelligent productivity assistance, at least in principle. A web-based interface with backend services and database management is being blended by this setup to support personal tasks and collaborative project workflows, and includes large language model-based AI assistance for daily planning, task guidance, and project intelligence, combining task-related information and deterministic processing with AI-generated explanations and recommendations. It also is stressing user control by requiring approval for AI-suggested changes before they're employed. PlanWise is built using React and Vite for the frontend and Supabase for authentication, database operations, and backend functionality, with Google Gemini API integration for AI-assisted attributes. This paper is outlining the system architecture, design methodology, implementation approach, and evaluation framework. In fact, the current implementation founds for integrating AI assistance into the personal and collaborative task management. Further testing is required for the assessment of the reliability, potency and concrete benefits of its AI-driven capabilities. Keywords—Artificial Intelligence, Task Management, Project Management, Large Language Models, Intelligent Planning, Human-AI Interaction

items.title: Platform Versus Creator Provision of Generative AI on Creator Platforms
items.abstract: Generative AI is changing not only how content is created on digital content platforms but also who provides the AI used to create it. Platforms may offer generative AI using data pooled across creators, whereas creators may provide AI services based on their own content. Understanding how these provision regimes affect creators’ investment incentives and the value generated by AI is therefore important. We develop a game-theoretic model in which human-generated content competes with AI-generated content while contributing to AI learning. The results show that platform provision can induce higher human-generated content quality than creator provision when AI learning effectiveness lies within a certain range and the platform’s pooled-data advantage is limited. A stronger pooled-data advantage can make creator provision more favorable for sustaining human-generated content quality. Platform provision can nevertheless generate higher AI-generated content quality even when creator provision induces higher human-generated content quality, provided that the pooled-data advantage is sufficiently strong. We further find that AI value sharing can encourage or discourage quality investment under platform provision, while its effects on regime preferences and preference alignment depend on market conditions. Thus, the provision regime preferred by the creator need not be the one that sustains higher human-generated content quality.

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

items.title: Pooled Prevalence of Infectious Diseases Among First Responders in the Prehospital Setting: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis by Occupation
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers.METHODS Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman–Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger’s regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool.RESULTS Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039.CONCLUSIONS Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

items.title: Precision Agriculture in the Digital Era: Integrating IoT, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Sustainable Crop Management
items.abstract: The increasing global population has intensified the demand for food, placing significant pressure on agricultural systems to enhance productivity while ensuring environmental sustainability. This review examines the integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in digital crop management, drawing on the technologies and applications discussed in the manuscript. Precision agriculture has emerged as an effective approach for optimising resource use by managing spatial and temporal variability within fields. It integrates advanced technologies such as the Global Positioning System, Geographic Information Systems, variable-rate technology, auto-steer guidance systems, wireless telematics, remote sensing, artificial intelligence and yield monitoring systems to support site-specific crop management. The adoption of the Internet of Things has further strengthened precision agriculture by enabling real-time monitoring of soil, crop and environmental parameters through sensor networks. These sensors generate continuous field data that facilitate informed decision-making and efficient resource utilisation. Furthermore, the large volume of data produced by IoT-based systems can be effectively analysed using machine learning techniques. As a subset of AI, ML enables the identification of patterns and generation of predictive insights for applications such as crop yield prediction, irrigation scheduling, nutrient management and weed detection, thereby enhancing productivity and sustainability in modern agriculture.

items.title: Predicting and interpreting the irradiation-induced tensile behavior of fast reactor cladding using explainable machine learning
items.abstract: HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels are promising candidates for advanced nuclear fuel cladding. In this study, 1,590 tensile test data points of 9–12Cr ferritic/martensitic (FM) steels were collected to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting irradiation-induced changes in the tensile properties of HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod). Regression models were evaluated after Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization using test-set evaluation and k -fold cross-validation (CV). Extreme gradient boosting (XGB) exhibited the best predictive performance; however, an artificial neural network (ANN) was selected for its continuous response, physical consistency, and stable representation of irradiation-dependent trends. Using independent experimental data, the ANN yielded mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 6.26 ± 0.47% for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and 10.69 ± 0.46% for yield strength (YS). The ANN model predicted the YS across irradiation conditions and showed that the irradiation-induced increase in YS for HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels saturated at 5–10 displacements per atom (dpa). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) method, quantified the contributions of dpa and irradiation temperature, revealing that irradiation temperature has a greater overall influence on the predicted YS. These results provide both reliable property predictions and physical insights into the effects of irradiation conditions.
